readout_other: c-Fos immunohistochemistry (Fos-positive/DAPI ratio); freezing during fear extinction and retention (ANY-maze); open field distance travelled
direction_notes: Fos expression rose in the infralimbic cortex but not adjacent regions after tFUS, and tFUS during extinction reduced freezing in extinction and retention, including after short-interval conditioning; open field activity was unchanged.
safety_notes: Authors report no discernible startle or sudden movements during open field sonication and no unusual behaviour during extinction; no histological damage assessment described.

exposures.label: tFUS to the infralimbic cortex (5 MHz head-mounted stimulator)

target.label: the infralimbic subdivision of the prefrontal cortex (IL)

device.manufacturer: Piezoelements, China (PZT disk); head-mounted stimulator fabricated in-house

timing.protocol_description: Pulsed sine waves (0.5 ms pulses at 1 kHz PRF) gated into bursts of 0.5 s with a 4.5 s inter-burst interval, total sonication 30 s per stimulation; applied concurrently with the CS during extinction (8 trials, or 20 in the immediate extinction experiment).

source_quotes.n_subjects: To investigate the effect of tFUS stimulation, two groups of rats $( \mathrm { t F U S : ~ n } = 1 1 ; \mathrm { S H A M : ~ n } = 1 1 )$ underwent fear conditioning, where 5 pairings of the CS and US were presented.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: Pulsed sine waves, with a resonant frequency of 5 MHz and a pulse duration (PD) of 0.5 m s, were repeated at a pulse repetition frequency (PRF) of 1 kHz and gated within square waves.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_duration_ms: Pulsed sine waves, with a resonant frequency of 5 MHz and a pulse duration (PD) of 0.5 m s, were repeated at a pulse repetition frequency (PRF) of 1 kHz and gated within square waves.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_repetition_fre: Pulsed sine waves, with a resonant frequency of 5 MHz and a pulse duration (PD) of 0.5 m s, were repeated at a pulse repetition frequency (PRF) of 1 kHz and gated within square waves.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: Each burst had a burst duration (BD) of 0.5 s and an inter-burst interval (IBI) of 4.5 s. The total sonication duration (SD) for one stimulation was 30 s
source_quotes.exposures[0].in_situ.isppa_w_cm2: A full width at half maximum (FWHM) beam size of $0 . 4 3 ~ \mathrm { m m } ^ { 3 }$ and a focal length of 1.8 mm were observed with a spatial peak pulse average intensity (I<sub>SPPA</sub>) of 1.53 W/ $\mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ at the focus, which was measured with an ex vivo rat skull (Fig. 1E).

flags.reason: 61 rats across Experiments 1-3 (17, 22, 22 analysed groups); some rats were also used in the open field test.
Intensity measured in a soybean oil tank through an ex vivo rat skull; classed in_situ measurement. No pressure or ISPTA given.
Total sonication duration of 30 s is built from 0.5 s bursts every 5 s (burst = a 0.5 s train of 0.5 ms pulses at 1 kHz); duty cycle not stated, not computed.
Only the Fos cell counting is stated to be done by an experimenter blinded to condition; recorded as single.
Sham reversed the PZT to control for auditory confounding; masking by the tone CS argued in the discussion; no direct measurement.
Healthy rats given fear conditioning and extinction (model of anxiety/PTSD therapy), no disease induced.
Stimulation on the extinction day (and an open field test two weeks later); total sessions not stated as a single number.
Head-mounted transducer assembled in-house from a PZT disk (Piezoelements, China) and a 3D-printed lens.
